title: Algebra of quantum mechanics \textit{via} classical phonons. II: Klein-Gordon dynamics, the Heisenberg formalism, the Dirac canonical commutation rule and the Poincaré algebra through the continuous Poisson bracket formalism
abstract: In the first part of this series we have shown how the Schrodinger equation for a single particle and the corresponding non relativistic quantum observables can be obtained from a purely classical phonon model through the Newtonian equations of motion. In this work we focus instead on how the classical Hamiltonian formalism applied to the same phonon system allows to recover the feature of relativistic quantum mechanics for a single spinless particle. Using the classical nature of the phonon model, we naturally define continuous Poisson brackets between classical observables, which allows to recover the dynamics of such observables, i.e. the Ehrenfest relations associated to real-valued Klein-Gordon fields. The Poisson brackets also permits to obtain the generic form of constants of motions, thus generalizing the concept of inner products and momentum on Klein-Gordon fields. We then connect the formalism of real-valued classical functionals with that of hermitian operators and complex-valued wave functions. This is done through the introduction of a non-local complex-valued change of variables which allows to rewrite the real-valued Klein-Gordon equation in a form akin to the Schrodinger equation, and the classical observables as quantum expectation values. Then, we show how this change of variables allows to rewrite the classical Poisson brackets as commutators of hermitian operators. This points out the strict equivalence between the Heisenberg formalism and the formalism of classical Poisson bracket. Eventually, we illustrate how the Poisson brackets allows to recover the transformations of Poincaré group in 1+1 dimension together with its algebra. The latter makes the link between the Lorentz invariant inner product of Mostafazadeh and the Casimir invariant associated to the mass of particle.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework to derive the core structures of quantum mechanics—including Klein-Gordon dynamics and Poincaré symmetry—entirely from a classical phonon model using Poisson brackets. It achieves this by demonstrating that a specific complex change of variables maps classical Poisson brackets directly onto fundamental quantum commutators, establishing deep formal equivalence between classical and quantum descriptions.
main_problem: The primary goal is to derive the full algebra of quantum mechanics, including Klein-Gordon dynamics and the Poincaré group structure, starting purely from a classical framework.
main_result: The paper establishes a strict mathematical equivalence between the Heisenberg formalism (quantum commutators) and the continuous Poisson bracket formalism by utilizing a non-local complex change of variables.
method: It employs the classical phonon model to define continuous Poisson brackets, which are then systematically related to quantum commutators via functional analysis and canonical quantization procedures.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a classical phonon lattice (related to the Frenkel-Kontorova model) whose continuum limit yields dynamics governed by equations leading to the Klein-Gordon equation. The formalism progresses from real-valued classical observables to complex quantum operators.
key_observables: Klein-Gordon fields, Poisson brackets $\{F, G\}$, commutators $[\hat{O}_F, \hat{O}_G]$, and Poincaré group generators ($H, X, P$).
important_parameters: The continuum limit parameters (e.g., $N	o\infty, a	o 0$) and the scaling factors used to connect classical variables to quantum operators are crucial.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on assuming that a non-local complex change of variables can bridge the gap between real-valued classical dynamics and complex quantum field theory structures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the physical lattice model (Frenkel-Kontorova) and later show abstract mathematical representations of group transformations using matrix forms for the Poincaré algebra generators.
paper_structure: The paper follows a progression: first establishing classical dynamics via phonons; then introducing Poisson brackets to derive Ehrenfest relations; next, performing a complex change of variables to link $\{., .\}$ to $[\cdot, \cdot]$; finally, applying this structure to recover the full Poincaré algebra in 1+1 dimensions.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly abstract and fundamental theoretical bridge between classical Hamiltonian mechanics (Poisson brackets) and quantum field theory (commutators), which is valuable for understanding quantization procedures beyond standard canonical methods.
